crime.value: Murder by ice-pick stabbing (32+ times); central question: why did a well-behaved, normal boy commit such a brutal killing, and is he legally/psychologically culpable?
crime.quote: he stabbed Laramer with an icepick. What was it—thirty-two times?

victim.value: Laramer, a drunk and abusive substitute father figure who beat both Richard Gorman and his mother, displaced Gorman's idealized dead father, and usurped his place in the household.
victim.quote: he was a lush, a drunken bum and he started beating hell out of me all the time...he didn't marry her, see, but he practically lived there, moved in, took over.

closed_world.value: Green Valley Manor psychiatric sanitarium, a private treatment facility where Gorman is confined and where the investigator Kessler has clinical authority and access.
closed_world.quote: Green Valley Manor resembled a lovely lakeside resort. Parklike grounds contained numerous small cottages...Here conditions were ideal for the advanced treatment of those who could be saved.

culprit_and_motive.value: Richard Gorman killed Laramer to purge an Oedipus (later Orestes) complex rooted in unconscious hatred of his father, displaced onto Laramer; Kessler—through therapy and literary suggestion—catalyzes Gorman's recognition of this motive, enabling further violence.
culprit_and_motive.quote: I hated him because he stood for my father. And I always unconsciously hated my father, because I was always jealous of his position with mother.

resolution.value: No traditional resolution. Gorman, psychologically 'cured' by Kessler's treatment, murders his mother during a sanitarium visit. Kessler discovers the body and realizes his own misogyny enabled the killing. The mystery ends with moral/psychological ambiguity and Kessler's recognition of complicity.
resolution.quote: It's odd, he thought, but it's the first time I ever could look upon a dead woman...I hated her too, he thought. I always hated women.

investigator.value: Dr. Kessler, a senior psychiatrist investigating not crime but psychology; he seeks to understand Gorman's motive, becomes his analyst and mentor, and inadvertently becomes complicit in enabling further murder through his theoretical framework.
investigator.quote: I'm interested in why he did it...Such cases as Gorman's could help illuminate one of the darkest cellars of psychiatry: the psychology of action.
